title: A constraint's own fields — software-analysis capability
description: The front matter of one constraint, a file `REQ-NNN-<slug>.md` in `requirements/constraints/` under the analysis location, optionally in a folder per functional area (software-analysis DEC-002 points 1 to 4): a limit on the solution, which the design takes as given. Its id is one numbering across the three kinds of requirement, so a requirement moved to another kind keeps it (point 2). The obligation, its measure and where it holds are fields a tool reads. Beside them, `obligation` holds their fingerprint, which a command writes (DEC-006 point 6). The body says what verifies it, and who or what imposes it. These are the constraint's own fields: its friction block sits in the methodology's container beside them and is the core's (COR-050, COR-053 point 10). Within the analysis it anchors each actor in `actors` and each requirement in `refines`, as artefact anchors (point 6). The three kinds' schemas take the same fields. Applied by `pkit software-analysis validate`; unknown fields are refused.

id.description: The constraint's id, `REQ-NNN`. It never changes, a move to another kind or another area included, and is never used again once the constraint is withdrawn (DEC-001 point 3, DEC-002 point 2).

title.description: The constraint's title, in a few words. The body's heading repeats it after the id and the kind, `# REQ-NNN · Constraint · <title>` (DEC-002 point 2). It may change; the id does not.

statement.description: The constraint, in one sentence: the limit the solution keeps (DEC-002 point 4). Its form, one sentence, is the kind's declared structure's, checked where the format rule binds.

measure.description: The value or the condition that shows the constraint is kept. It reads `None.` where there is none yet, so the gap is seen (DEC-002 point 4).

applies-to.description: Where the constraint holds, in words, such as a class of commands or the whole system. It never reads `None.`, which the kind's declared structure refuses where the format rule binds. It names no use case or journey: those that must meet the constraint list it (DEC-002 points 4 and 7).

obligation.description: The fingerprint of the constraint's statement, its measure and where it holds, which `pkit analysis obligation` writes and the check holds equal to them, whatever any rule's status: `v<version>:sha256:<digest>`, the version of the form its texts are read in, the hash, then the digest (software-analysis DEC-006 points 6 and 7). Never written by hand. The check fails a constraint without it, one whose value is no fingerprint, and one whose value no longer matches its texts, and names the command.

actors.description: The actors whose need the constraint meets, by id. Each is an artefact anchor of the constraint (DEC-002 point 6), but an actor of an analysis it builds on, named with that analysis, whose records it anchors instead (DEC-001 point 2). Absent, or empty, where it meets no actor's need.

refines.description: The requirements it refines, of any kind, by id. Each is an artefact anchor of the constraint, and a chain of them that comes back to it closes a cycle, which validation refuses (DEC-002 point 6; COR-050 point 5). Absent, or empty, where it refines none.
